purpose: Re-extract published aggregate evidence relevant to non-COVID healthcare access from three primary research articles. This is not a reconstruction of patient-level or hospital-level raw datasets.
policy: New source-derived evidence only; no legacy processed CSVs or previously transformed values were used as inputs.

sources.citation: Yoshida S, Okubo R, Katanoda K, Tabuchi T. Impact of state of emergency for coronavirus disease 2019 on hospital visits and disease exacerbation: the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey. Family Practice. 2022;39(5):883-890. doi:10.1093/fampra/cmac016.
sources.access_status: publisher_full_text_html_read; PMC lists supplementary DOC and DOCX, not downloaded; participant-level dataset not public
sources.source_data_access: Data underlying the article cannot be shared publicly due to ethics approval restrictions.
sources.extracted_content: Methods, Tables 1-3, results, data availability statement; 14 aggregate rows.
limitations: Cross-sectional self-report survey; data collection 2020-08-25 to 2020-09-30 with recall of April-May 2020.
Analysis restricted to 7,747 respondents reporting a disease currently under treatment from the 28,000-person JACSIS sample.
Participant-level dataset unavailable publicly; article aggregates and supplementary table only.
No acute-care or mortality outcomes; findings are not causal.

sources.citation: Yamaguchi S, Okada A, Sunaga S, et al. Impact of COVID-19 pandemic on healthcare service use for non-COVID-19 patients in Japan: retrospective cohort study. BMJ Open. 2022;12:e060390. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2021-060390.
sources.access_status: publisher_full_text_PDF_read; ten supplementary PDFs listed by PMC but not downloaded; underlying MDV claims dataset not public
sources.source_data_access: MDV dataset is proprietary to Medical Data Vision and not publicly available for research; article says it may be purchased from MDV.
sources.extracted_content: Methods, Results, figures and text-reported outcome values; 31 aggregate rows.
limitations: 26 anonymised hospitals; facility locations and infection status unknown.
Study cohort includes patients with at least one serum creatinine measurement, potentially underrepresenting less serious outpatients.
Hospitalisation counts are based on monthly discharges, not admission dates.
Percent changes are 2020 vs 2019, not national rates.
Decreases can reflect changed disease incidence, behaviour, thresholds, patient avoidance, or hospital capacity; cannot be attributed to access restrictions alone.

sources.citation: Kurokawa T, Ozaki A, Bhandari D, et al. Association between COVID-19 incidence and postponement or cancellation of elective surgeries in Japan until September 2020: a cross-sectional, web-based survey. BMJ Open. 2022;12:e059886. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2021-059886.
sources.access_status: publisher_full_text_PDF_read; no supplementary file identified in retrieved publisher/PMC records; underlying data available upon reasonable request, not requested
sources.source_data_access: Data available upon reasonable request; no direct request made.
sources.extracted_content: Methods, Table 2/3 and Results; unweighted and weighted reported estimates stored separately.
limitations: Nationwide web-based self-report survey; 3,678 participants with planned elective surgery.
The unweighted raw count (223/3,678; 6.06%) and weighted estimate (431/3,678; 11.72%) are distinct and must not be merged.
Surgical conditions were not collected; severity and appropriateness of postponement cannot be assessed.
No normal-period comparator, so the causal effect of the pandemic or emergency declaration cannot be isolated.

extraction_controls: All reported percentages, counts, odds ratios and confidence intervals retain their article-specific unit and estimation basis.
No daily or monthly time series was created from cross-sectional survey results.
No missing raw counts were reverse-engineered from rounded percentages.
No facility-level or participant-level observations were imputed.
Source-reported aggregate values are not described as independently re-calculated from raw claims or survey microdata.
Supplementary file presence is distinguished from successful file download and content-level verification.

supplementary_material_audit.scope: Availability and bibliographic audit of supplementary files; file contents were not transcribed because direct file retrieval was blocked/unavailable in this pass.

yoshida_2022.note: Oxford Academic article page did not expose a supplementary-data link in the retrieved article view. PMC indexed full-text/associated-data result explicitly lists both files. Actual binary download and content inspection remain outstanding.

yamaguchi_2022.note: The main article refers to supplementary figures/tables and ICD-10 code definitions. The ten PDFs themselves were not downloaded; their individual contents and exact filename-to-table/figure mapping remain unverified.

kurokawa_2022.source: BMJ Open publisher full-text PDF and PMC/PubMed indexed records
kurokawa_2022.note: The publisher full-text PDF was inspected. It refers to online prepublication history but contains no supplementary-material section or supplementary-file references in the retrieved PDF text. PMC/PubMed searches did not surface a supplementary-file listing in this pass. This is not proof that no supplemental file exists anywhere. Data are available upon reasonable request; no request was made.
